The files in this folder are airfield weather reports (METAR) as the
Aviation Weather Center of the United States' National Weather Service
publishes them, https://aviationweather.gov/data/api/. The reports are
written by the weather offices of the airfields, here in Germany, Austria,
Switzerland, Italy, Slovenia and Hungary, and exchanged between the
world's aviation weather services; the centre decodes and serves them. Its
site's disclaimer, https://www.weather.gov/disclaimer, says of the
information on the service's pages that it is "in the public domain,
unless specifically noted otherwise", and may be used for any lawful
purpose by whoever does not claim it as their own, imply an endorsement by
the service, or present changed content as official. The files are not
covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-21 from https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/,
without a key, with curl under a user agent of its own.

    metar.json              GET /metar?bbox=46.3,9.4,48.5,17.2&format=json
                            at 10:37:30 UTC: the whole answer to the
                            adapter's request for the first region,
                            unchanged. 22 reports, 9,586 bytes.
    metar_2026-11-18.json   the same request with
                            &date=2026-11-18T19:05:00Z, asked at
                            10:39:00 UTC: the whole answer, unchanged. 20
                            reports, 8,667 bytes. The adapter never asks
                            with a date.

metar_evening.json is NOT an answer of the service as it gave one. It is a
sample for the server's development mode, whose clock stands at 19:05 UTC
on 2026-11-18, three days before this source was recorded: three reports
of metar_2026-11-18.json, those of EDJA (Memmingen), LOWI (Innsbruck) and
LSZS (Samedan), each byte for byte as the service wrote it, in the
answer's form. All three are of 18:50 UTC and reached the service between
18:52 and 18:56 UTC, so the service had them at the moment of that clock.
A test of this crate holds the sample against the answer it is cut from.

metar_damaged.json is not the service's data: it is six entries, five of
them reports of metar_2026-11-18.json changed by hand and one that is no
report, to test how the adapter reports what it cannot read. The test that
uses it says what was changed.

To record them again: fetch the first address and replace metar.json; set
the moment in tests/pipeline.rs; run the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1
and review what changed. The values the test pins are of that moment and
will differ. The evening sample stays as it is for as long as the
development mode's clock does. The service keeps thirty days, so the
answer for 2026-11-18 cannot be fetched again after 2026-12-18.

A METAR is the weather at an airfield, written for aircraft that land
there. It is no statement about the air at a take-off, and none that a
place can be flown.
